summary:
# NOTES: *The Mystery at Lovers' Cave* by Anthony Berkeley (Gutenberg #70877; 1927 Simon & Schuster ed.)

Single book, 26 chapters. Narrated third person, mostly from Anthony's and Roger's viewpoints. Comic detective tone.

## Cast
- **Roger Sheringham**: novelist/amateur sleuth, 36, bachelor flat. Witty, self-satisfied, pipe smoker. Freelance Special Correspondent for the *Daily Courier* (editor is "that great man"; reporter Burgoyne phoned him). Prior case: Wychford affair / "Hattan Garden jewel case" with Mr. Turner of the *Courier*. Calls women by Christian names. Ends up embarrassed by his leak to the *Courier*.
- **Anthony Walton**: cousin, 25 (Roger is ~10+ years older; Roger says "nearly a dozen years"). Big, broad-shouldered, slow-witted, good-natured. Oxford rugger blue; plays for Harlequins; half-blue for golf; works in father's office. Falls for Margaret. Calls Roger "idiot friend" role. Pipe smoker.
- **Inspector Moresby**: Scotland Yard, heavily built, grizzled walrus moustache, butter-knife face, bland, genial, jovial. Holidaying at Sandsea with wife and two children; takes room at the Crown. Officially in charge of case from headquarters. Says "Hell!" occasionally; quotes "Haw, haw." Enjoys whisky, ginger-beer and gin; "tankards."
- **Margaret Cross**: 22ish, dark hair in two coils, brown eyes, black frock, "unshingled." Cousin of Mrs. Vane (her mother was Elsie's mother's sister—actually Elsie's mother was Margaret's mother's sister). Father an army officer killed in France 1917 when she was 15. Mother was daughter of Liverpool bucket-shop man, "married beneath" him. Trained as shorthand-typist; worked as governess, shop assistant, waitress, parlour-maid (dismissed after boxing an employer's ears). Given a letter by Elsie; lives at Dr. Vane's house as companion. Elsie's will left her £10,000+ and jewellery (later invalidated). She reports being alone at the cliff, waiting ~1.5 hours.
- **Elsie Vane (Mrs. Vane)**: victim, 28. Fell from Ludmouth Bay cliffs. Married Dr. George Vane ~5 years earlier, for money; her real name/family was criminal (grandfather/great-grandfather burglars; her father was with wholesale chemists; father died when she was 17; she'd been in shoplifting and gambling-joint decoy work). Little, fragile, babyish face, fair hair, lisp, pretends helplessness. Real surname was not Vane: she went through a form of marriage with Herbert Peters during the war (per police). Bullied Margaret. Smoked Turkish cigarettes (pink tips) and ate chocolates in the cave.
- **Dr. George Vane**: big man, 6'2", huge black beard, stern eye, gentle movements. Retired/former doctor, now experimental scientist with laboratory at back of house. Fine china collector (Spode, Dresden). Courteous to Elsie. Asks Roger and Anthony to supper on Sunday; has "very devil of a temper."
- **Miss Mary Williamson**: Dr. Vane's secretary/laboratory assistant. Tall, angular, close-cropped fair hair, pince-nez, cold blue eyes; Cambridge science degree. In love with Dr. Vane. Had an alibi-gap that Tuesday afternoon (out on cliffs ~half hour).
- **Mr. John Henry Russell** (Rose Cottage): jolly, red-faced, beefy; alleged to be too friendly with Elsie. Has cast-iron alibi.
- **Mrs. Russell**: fat, decided, pince-nez, hair greying, ~45, large feet; hated Elsie; cut Margaret dead. Her shoes were the ones used to fake footprints.
- **Colin Woodthorpe**: son of Sir Henry Woodthorpe (Clouston Hall, Georgian house, 9–10 acres); ex-RAF; owns aeroplane. Elsie's lover ~1 year; broke with her at cave meeting "a fortnight ago last Tuesday." Letter signed "Colin." Engaged secretly to Margaret. Butler is a "dolphin." Confessed falsely to murders at inn; then eloped by aeroplane with Margaret.
- **Rev. Samuel Meadows** ("goat-faced clergyman," silvery hair, horn spectacles, benign, talkative, "retired" in Ludmouth few weeks): actually Sam Field, alias Slippery Sam, The Shrimp, The Sky Pilot, Herbert Peters, Herbert Smith. Criminal record (robbery 1909–11; burglary 1913–16; fraud 1918–23). Mole on right cheek, blue eyes, large nose. Lodged with Mrs. Harper (stout landlady, toothache night, "Mrs. Mullins" friend). Found dead in sitting-room chair with aconitine in pipe stem; murdered.
- **Mrs. Jameson**: Ludmouth woman expecting visitors (mentioned).
- **Landlord of the Crown** (Ludmouth inn): large, ox-like, perspiring; sells only lemonade/ginger-beer/beer. "Combined porter/station-master/ticket-inspector" at Ludmouth station (comic).
- **Dr. Young**: local doctor, tall, angular, pince-nez.
- **Mr. Simpson**: the Coroner, fussy.
- **Sir Henry Griffen**: Home Office analyst.
- **Burgoyne**: Daily Courier caller.
- Constable (unnamed, red jaw, nose-blowing).
- Fisherman (unnamed, "dratted girl being tickled").

## Places
- London: Roger's flat (Greene = servant); St. Pancras; Waterloo.
- Route: Waterloo → Bournemouth (change) → Ludmouth station (~1 mile from village).
- Ludmouth village: one pub, the Crown; Ludmouth Bay, almost circular inlet, cliffs ~100 ft; steep track to village.
- Sandsea: town ~6 miles west; Inspector's holiday; Three Swans inn (over a mile outside village).
- Vane house: red-brick, a mile or so out Sandsea way, in own grounds back from cliffs. Russells' house (Rose Cottage) between Vane house and village.
- Ledge: about a third down cliff face; flight of steps cut at each end; hidden from clifftop by bulge. Mud patch with two sets of footprints (women's; larger pair). Body wedged between two rocks ("big rock with seaweed and yellow limpets") a couple of feet above high-water, beyond a deep pool.
- Cave: small, entered by angled opening masked by boulder; ~10 ft wide x 12 deep; ledge-couch; cigarettes, chocolate boxes, banana skins, copy of *London Opinion* (last Saturday's issue).
- Clouston Hall: Woodthorpe's home.
- Ludmouth Mystery: name of case.

## Chronology
**Day 1 (Monday, per letter "Monday")**: Roger at breakfast in London with Anthony; telephone from Burgoyne; Roger switches holiday (Derbyshire → Hampshire/Ludmouth). Train 12:10 from Waterloo; lunch on train. Arrive Ludmouth; Crown: five rooms booked, £10 deposit. Roger sends Anthony to find Miss Cross. Roger meets Moresby on ledge; footprints; sees the button (Moresby holds it back). Roger descends to rocks, finds crumpled notepaper ("Colin" letter) under handkerchief—pocket. Evening: supper with Moresby; Moresby reveals a light-blue bone button with white pattern found clenched in Elsie's hand, identified as from Margaret's sports coat.
- Anthony meets Margaret on ledge (before Roger); she tearfully confides (Inspector questioned her two hours that morning). Her story: father died France 1917; mother a bucket-shop daughter; her own jobs; Elsie's invitation; will for £10,000+.

**Day 2 (Tuesday)**: Roger/Anthony/Margaret meet on ledge at 10:30. Margaret's account: walked toward Sandsea, returned; Elsie left her near Russells' (Mrs. Russell) and never arrived; Margaret waited ~1.5 hrs. Roger finds the Colin letter (text given: "Elsie darling... Meet me at the usual place to-morrow, same time... Colin. P.S. Destroy this."; dated Monday). Roger visits Moresby; supper with whisky; Moresby uncovers letter's text. Colin = Russell? No: directory lists John Henry Russell at Rose Cottage; Colin Woodthorpe later found. Roger interviews Mr. Meadows (parson) on cliffs, who reveals name rumours about Margaret; Roger later steals Mrs. Russell's shoes via her parlour maid (Rose cottage) and matches them to footprints. Margaret reveals Elsie was loathsome; Russell affair; Mrs. Russell jealous. Mrs. Russell's shoes fit prints (Roger's "solution" #1—Mrs. Russell pushed Elsie).
- Afternoon: Roger tea-party at Dr. Vane's house with Margaret, Anthony, Miss Williamson; supper invitation for following Sunday. Roger/Anthony meet Moresby; Moresby identifies Colin Woodthorpe (through directory/search).
- Evening: Roger and Moresby interview Colin Woodthorpe at Clouston Hall. Woodthorpe admits affair; cave meeting "a fortnight ago last Tuesday"; broke off; Elsie threatened to tell husband (would mean divorce). Roger and Moresby discuss; Moresby reveals Elsie's criminal past (Herbert Peters etc.).

**Day 3 (Wednesday)**: Midnight expedition (Roger+Anthony) to cave; find *London Opinion* last Saturday's issue (contradicts Colin). Morning: Roger tests Colin (joke). Roger's theory: unknown middle-class man. Afternoon: Margaret tells of Elsie's fear; Roger deduces the shoe found on rock (a lady's size 6, slit sides, buckle torn). Moresby intervenes; claims cave-search and shoe; Moresby's theory: Miss Williamson. Roger's child-witness: a man with a paper seen going down to ledge at 3:30 pm Tuesday. Roger tricks Rev. Meadows into giving thumbprint.

**Day 4 (Thursday)**: Thumbprint sent by telephone code/report: match to Sam Field alias Herbert Peters etc. Roger & Moresby arrive at Meadows' lodgings; Meadows found dead in chair. Dr. Young (doctor) examines. Roger's indiscreet telephone call to Courier revealed arrest plan—inspector angry.

**Following days**: Inquest adjourned; poison found: aconitine (in tobacco-jar and pipe-stem). Roger's second theory: Elsie poisoned Meadows posthumously (Elsie had visited Meadows' room ~3 weeks earlier; handkerchief marked "E"; Meadows changed pipes weekly, Sunday). Anthony reports Margaret's secret engagement (per inspector). Inspector had been pressing Margaret; Margaret and Colin elope by aeroplane. Colin came to inn to confess to double murder (falsely). Inspector's final twist: Margaret killed Elsie (coat-button; shoe-swap; she planted Mrs. Russell's shoes), and killed Meadows (aconitine in pipe, Sunday night). Official verdicts: accidental (Elsie) and suicide (Meadows). Inspector: Elsie's marriage settlement invalid (not legal wife); Margaret gets no £10,000. Last line: "You've been reading too many of those detective stories."

## Key Objects / Quotes
- Button: light-blue bone, white pattern, ~1.5 inch; from Margaret's sports-coat; clenched in Elsie's right hand.
- Footprints: two women's pairs; larger pair belongs to Mrs. Russell's shoes (size 6? the shoe found is size six).
- Letter: "Elsie darling, for Heaven's sake meet me once more before you do anything rash..." signed "Colin"; "P.S. Destroy this."
- Cigarettes: Turkish with pink tips; gaspers.
- *London Opinion*, last Saturday's issue (found in cave, Colin's appointment-side question).
- Shoe: lady's size six; buckle torn; sides slit.
- Thumbprint: right thumb of Sam Field.
- Aconitine: found in tobacco-jar and pipe stem; at least a grain.
- Handkerchief: fine cambric, lace edging, small embroidered "E."
- Roger's Courier articles; "Do Shingled Heads Mean Shingled Hearts?"; "Clergymen Who Gabble" letter.
- Inspector's line: "Footprints are the easiest thing in the world to fake."
- Crown lemonade-only stance; Roger books five rooms (deposit £10: two five-pound notes).

## Miscellaneous
- Ludmouth station porter jokes ("best pub"; "only one").
- Roger's cricket reference: Kent all out 47 on plumb wicket at Blackheath.
- Anthony's stated faith: games matter; Margaret: "Poor Anthony!"
- Roger's nickname "Oyster" at school; Roger calls Anthony "fair coz," "bandicoot."
- Woodthorpe's butler "the dolphin."
- Russell's maid: unnamed; cook takes the *Courier*.
